mappings.note: Contrasts the two monsoons by the direction of flow and the moisture each carries - atmospheric circulation. Not LO-27, because the item is about the wind regimes rather than mapping where the rain lands.
Surfacing deep-sea fish and the flowering Golden Shower tree as local monsoon indicators is knowledge built by people living in a climate. Not LO-26, because no mechanism is explained.

The question asks explicitly for the immediate impact on people - agriculture hit, women walking farther for water, labour migration. That human-consequence emphasis is LO-28; the bare definition items on monsoon failure were given LO-29.
Cyclone formation over warm seas through low pressure and inrushing moist air is an atmospheric process. Not LO-29, because no warning or response is asked for.
Clouds as suspended droplets and ice crystals is the moisture content of the atmosphere. Not LO-27, since nothing is located.

Why the Gangetic plains flood in the monsoon - runoff exceeding river capacity - is the causal analysis behind flood preparedness. Not LO-27, because the item is about a hazard, not the region's normal climate.
A glacial burst explained through a failing moraine dam and the devastating flood below. The hazard lane; LO-25 would be wrong because no landform is being built.
Overburdened drains, blocked waterways and impermeable surfaces as the causes of urban flooding. Not LO-30: the failure is drainage, not pollution.
Landslide triggers plus the Indian regions most at risk - hazard causes and their geography. Not LO-27, because the regions are listed as vulnerable, not as climatic types.
Drought, wind and human carelessness as causes of forest fires. Hazard causation, the same lane as the landslide and flood items.

The natural greenhouse effect - gases holding enough of the sun's heat to make the Earth habitable - is a property of the atmosphere's composition. Not LO-30, which is kept for the human intensification of it, asked in the very next item.

Fossil fuels, deforestation and industry releasing excess greenhouse gases is an analysis of what humans are doing to the air. Deliberately distinguished from the previous item, which asked about the natural effect.

Mitigation defined as cutting emissions, with tree planting and renewables as examples - measures against the pollution of the atmosphere. Not LO-29, which covers coping with a disaster rather than removing its cause.
Srinagar against Kanniyakumari worked out purely through latitude and the angle of the sun's rays - the control that sets climatic belts. Not LO-28, because neither city's people appear.

Coastal Mumbai's narrow annual range against inland Nagpur's wide one, explained by the sea - a maritime-continental comparison. Not LO-26, because the contrast is between two places, not inside the atmosphere.
Windward rainfall and the Deccan rain shadow is the geographical distribution of monsoon rain. Not LO-26: the uplift mechanism is summarised, but the question asks why one side is drier.

The 'double-edged sword' argument needs both the monsoon as the basis of agriculture and the economy (LO-28) and its failure or excess producing drought and flood (LO-29). Neither half alone carries the statement.

Deforestation and hillside cutting raising landslide risk is hazard causation with a clear preventive implication. Not LO-31, because the argument is about slope stability rather than about valuing the forest itself.

Forest fires are weighed both as a disaster with economic losses (LO-29) and as destruction of habitat, wildlife and air quality (LO-31). The environmental half of the expected answer is squarely the conservation outcome.

The full chain from burning fossil fuels to excess CO2 to rapid warming, and why that matters. The clearest causes-of-atmospheric-degradation item in the chapter; LO-26 would reduce it to the natural greenhouse effect.

Warming making floods, droughts, heat waves and cyclones more frequent and severe is about the hazard regime a community must prepare for. Not LO-30, because the emissions cause is assumed and the disasters are the subject.
Climate knowledge feeding early warning systems, cyclone shelters and flood barriers is preventive action stated directly. Not LO-27, because the climate pattern is the input, not the answer.
The NDRF's rescue, evacuation and pre-positioning role in cyclones, floods and landslides is disaster response. No other code in this frame touches emergency machinery.
Compares a natural mountain flood cause with a largely human urban one - two routes to the same disaster. Not LO-27, because neither setting is treated as a climatic region.
Baisakhi and Pongal as harvest festivals timed to the seasonal cycle is the fullest climate-and-culture item in the chapter. Not LO-27, since no region is located.

Explains how an urban heat island forms as a microclimate warmer than its rural surroundings. Kept with the microclimate items; the answer turns on surfaces, waste heat and lost evapotranspiration rather than on pollutants, so LO-30 would misplace it.

The clash is between cutting fossil-fuel use and regulating industry (LO-30) and the long-term environmental need set against short-term economic gain, which is the sensitivity LO-31 asks for. Not LO-29, because no disaster is in view.

The argument rests on India's range of climatic regions (LO-27) and on how differently agriculture and water use work in each of them (LO-28). A single code would drop either the diversity or the livelihood half.

Predicting December-January conditions in Shimla, Jaipur and Goa is applying knowledge of three climatic regions. Not LO-28, because the tourists are a framing device and no resident population is discussed.

All three parts trace a failed monsoon through crop loss, food prices and socio-economic strain on the farming community - climate acting on livelihoods. Not LO-29, because no warning, relief or preventive measure is requested.

Part (iii) asks outright for a preventive measure against future landslides (LO-29), while part (ii) turns on tree roots binding the slope, which is the case for keeping forest cover (LO-31). Both halves are examined.
A red cyclone alert, the dangers, evacuation and the NDRF's role - preventive action end to end. Not LO-26, because the storm's physics never comes up.

Coal to CO2 to warming and drought, closing with a mitigation strategy - causes of atmospheric degradation and the measures against them. Not LO-29, because the droughts are a predicted consequence rather than an event being prepared for.
